title: skills: a published project-process skill for metadata apps — areas and grades, first touch, which document at which stage, testing and acceptance
body:
repo:hotcrm#3 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbXSZrwmusBcL7dnLQf

Part of objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2661 (child 5 of the hotcrm priorities rollout objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2656), item 7.

## Why

Maintainer rulings, verbatim (2026-11-18, hotcrm priorities thread):
- 16:09Z 「这个项目中的很多做法应该是元数据项目的最佳实践，是不是应该写到平台的skills中，跟着技能安装到元数据项目中国呢」
- 16:10Z 「ok」
- 16:14Z 「这个skills是整个元数据项目的核心指引，用 fable 综合评估一下需要些什么」

The 12 published skills teach how to write metadata. None teaches how to run a metadata-app project. Today the scaffold and the skills disagree on how an app tests itself: `skills/objectstack-platform/references/operations.md` teaches `LiteKernel`, while the scaffold's sample test uses `@objectstack/verify` `bootStack` (`packages/create-objectstack/src/templates/blank/note.test.ts`). No skill mentions `@objectstack/verify`.

Scope below follows an independent review. The review is in the project files; its verdicts are restated here.

## v1 — `skills/objectstack-project` (process domain, `SKILL.md` under ~200 lines)

1. **Two opening questions.** Does this belong in the app or in the platform? Is the app for own use, or a product shipped to customers? The heavier parts apply only to a product; the light path is the default.
2. **Stage × document table.** This is the skeleton: requirement, design, card, build, test and acceptance, user docs, release, upgrade.
3. **Test boundary.** The app pins business facts with `@objectstack/verify`. It does not hand-write checks the platform derives. The skill lists what this version's `os validate`, `os lint` and verify actually check, so an agent never skips a check nobody runs. Plugin tests stay in objectstack-platform; one home per rule (#31112).
4. **Platform gaps.** Never worked around in the app. File the card upstream; the app card waits until the fix is released into the app's pin.
5. **Changes written for customers.** Release notes come from changesets. A breaking change says from what to what, which platform version it needs, and the customer's steps.
6. **Bumping the pin and data migration.** Bump `@objectstack/*` together, re-sync the skills, sweep the waiting cards. Backfill scripts run before the upgrade, only through REST, and report by default (hotcrm's 8 `scripts/backfill-*.ts`). Retiring app tests once a platform check takes over follows hotcrm's `RETIRED` markers.
7. **Pointers** to the 12 domain skills.
- `description` names tasks, not file names (#34769): starting a feature or fix, filing or grading a card, opening a PR, cutting a release, bumping the platform.
- Evals include scenarios: a platform defect found; asked to hand-write a reference-integrity test; a business-fact test; dropping a field; a pin bump; and a counter-example, a one-person app changing a label, which must not demand a requirement record.

## Scaffold, same epic

- `ci.yml` runs `pnpm test`. Today it does not, although the README tells users to.
- The template AGENTS.md gets five lines pointing at the skill. Its hand-written skill table goes; it lists 9 of 12 skills. Copilot and Cursor read only AGENTS.md.
- A three-line PR template: what a user can do now, how it was checked, whether the docs changed.
- No empty `docs/PRIORITIES.md` or `docs/requirements/`. The skill carries the templates and creates them the first time they are needed, for new and old apps alike.

## Later

- `references/triage.md`: areas, first touch and grades as a fill-in.
- `references/growth.md`: growing from one package to an app plus modules.
- A docs-site guide whose stage table is generated from the skill.
- A tag-time changeset check as a platform command.
- A reusable workflow.

## Not published

- Seats, `pm:*` states, Tier and review levels, `reach:` lines: fleet machinery.
- A/B/C/D dispositions as a general requirement.
- hotcrm's own standards (three-locale docs, one e2e per chain) and any hotcrm area content.

## Open

- Grade and when it runs: for the maintainer.
- Unverified: whether `experimental_sync` brings a newly added skill into an installed app. Check this on a real app first.
- `skills/**` is governed: Tier H, os-zhuang approves.

## Done when

- `@objectstack/skills` ships the skill with its evals.
- A freshly scaffolded app runs its tests in CI and its AGENTS.md points at the skill.
- hotcrm's `docs/PRIORITIES.md` keeps only hotcrm's own content.
